headline: Thief Returns Stolen $290,000 Watch With Apology Note; Police Unsure Whether to Arrest or Thank Him
subheadline: The Audemars Piguet was posted back to the Tokyo boutique with a written apology, leaving detectives in the awkward position of investigating a crime that has already apologised for itself.
author: Margaret Pemberton-Smythe, Chief Absurdity Correspondent
seoTitle: Thief Returns Stolen Watch With Apology Note in Japan | The Daily Absurd
seoDescription: Satire: a Tokyo shoplifter returned a $290,000 watch with an apology note. Police describe the case as 'almost too polite to prosecute'.
sourceEvent: A customer who tried on a ¥-equivalent $290,000 Audemars Piguet watch at a Tokyo store left with it, and the watch was later returned to the store with an apology note from the thief — reported among the year's most Japanese stories.

social.x: A thief in Tokyo stole a $290,000 watch, then mailed it back with an apology note. The crime has apologised for itself. The justice system has no procedure for this.
social.facebook: Only in Japan: shoplifter takes $290,000 watch, feels bad, posts it back with a written apology. Detectives now reviewing whether politeness is a legal defence.
social.instagram: He stole a $290k watch. He sent it back. With a note. With proper handwriting. #satire #japan
altHeadlines: Crime Rates Plummet After Criminals Start Apologising
Watch Returned With Apology; Apology Described as 'Genuinely Heartfelt'

body:
Tokyo police are grappling with what legal scholars call 'an unprecedented crisis of courtesy' after a thief returned a stolen $290,000 Audemars Piguet watch to the boutique it was taken from — accompanied by a written apology.

The timepiece vanished earlier this month when a customer asked to try it on, then simply left, still wearing it, in what witnesses described at the time as 'a bold move' and have since revised to 'a bold move with a conscience'.

Days later, the watch arrived back at the store, in good condition, with a note of apology. The note's contents have not been fully disclosed, though a source close to the investigation confirmed it was 'sincere', 'well-composed' and 'written with noticeably good penmanship'.

"We are proceeding with the investigation," said a police spokesperson, in the tone of a man who had rehearsed the sentence several times. "The property was taken unlawfully and returned voluntarily with remorse. Our guidelines are…" he paused, "…quiet on this scenario."

Retail security experts say the incident sets a troubling precedent for the criminal justice system, which has standard procedures for theft, fraud and armed robbery, but none whatsoever for 'grand larceny, but then felt awful about it'.

"If word gets out that returning stolen goods with a note reduces your sentence," warned one criminologist, "we could see a wave of extremely polite crime. Burglars leaving thank-you cards. Art thieves including a gift receipt. Society as we know it could become slightly more pleasant."

The boutique has declined to comment beyond confirming the watch is back in its case, where staff say it now 'ticks with what can only be described as humility'.

At press time, the thief remained at large, presumed apologetic.
